collection_summary:
Original `top_k` instance that **chips top_k from gap 2 to gap 1** (4 of 5 staged after this instance; one more saturates the 6th category). **Transportation/Logistics NEW subdomain** — the Transportation family extends from 1 instance (`countries_that_drive_on_the_left`, Transportation/Road Traffic) to 2 instances with a NEW Logistics subdomain, making Transportation a 2-subdomain family. Natural human query: 'What are the world's busiest container ports — how many containers does each handle annually, what country and city is each in, and what world region?'

Multi-wiki source plan (21 URLs): 1 Wikipedia 'List of busiest container ports' master article supplies the universe + ranking + TEU value (the master article's 2024 column is sourced from Lloyd's List 'One Hundred Container Ports 2025' retrieved 2025-09-18 and cross-referenced with World Shipping Council); 20 per-port Wikipedia articles supply per-row Country + City via infobox/lead. Region is a curator-assigned closed-vocabulary categorical.

Result: 20 rows × 5 columns (Port PK + Country categorical + City categorical + TEU (millions) numeric + Region categorical), single-key PK on Port, 0 duplicates. Country distribution: China 9 (dominates modern container-port rankings — Shanghai, Ningbo-Zhoushan, Shenzhen, Qingdao, Guangzhou, Tianjin, Hong Kong, Xiamen, Suzhou), Malaysia 2 (Port Klang + Tanjung Pelepas), United States 2 (Los Angeles + Long Beach), plus singletons for Singapore, South Korea, UAE, Netherlands, Belgium, Morocco, Thailand (10 distinct countries). Region distribution: East Asia 10, Southeast Asia 4, Europe 2, North America 2, Middle East 1, Africa 1 (6 distinct regions out of the 9-value declared vocabulary; South Asia, Latin America, and Oceania declared but unused in staged top-20). TEU range: 9.6 (Laem Chabang) to 51.5 (Shanghai) — 41.9 M TEU span.

Universe rule: top-20 container ports by 2024 annual TEU throughput per Wikipedia 'List of busiest container ports' master article's 2024 column. All 20 are operational as of source-access date 2026-05-14 (no construction-status exclusions; the master article does not maintain an under-construction split for ports — all ranked entries are active operational ports). Master ranking is the universe authority; per-port articles supply non-time-series attribute values only.

Entity class: `organizations/ports` (NEW fine-class in the `organizations` bucket — bucket extends from 3 to 4 instances after this Ready, joining universities + companies + space-agencies).

**Canonical-source rule INVERSION** (carried forward from cycle-2-bridges + cycle-2-dams precedent with explicit inversion documented): for time-series throughput metrics (TEU), the master article wins for value because the master has annual update cadence (Lloyd's List 2024) while per-port Wikipedia article infoboxes are years out of date (Shanghai infobox 43.3M from 2019; Guangzhou body 4.774M from 2006; Hong Kong infobox 18M from 2020; Ningbo-Zhoushan body 16.83M from 2012 — all stale by 3-10 years). For non-time-series attributes (Country, City), per-port article wins (entity-detail role). The bridges/dams per-entity-wins rule applied to static structural metrics (Main Span, Height); this ports instance flips the rule for time-series metrics (TEU) where master has freshness advantage. This is a domain-specific refinement of the canonical-source rule, documented at Stage-1 so future audit cycles do not re-litigate the inversion.
source_coverage_notes:
Twenty-one Wikipedia source URLs combine. One 'List of busiest container ports' master article defines the universe + ranking + 2024 TEU values (Lloyd's List sourced); 20 per-port articles supply per-row Country + City via infobox/lead. Region is a curator-assigned closed-vocabulary categorical not directly sourced from the per-port articles.

Roles:
- source_urls[0] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_busiest_container_ports): universe + ranking + value (TEU 2024). Master article maintains TEU columns for 2004-2024; the 2024 column is sourced from Lloyd's List 'One Hundred Container Ports 2025' (retrieved 2025-09-18) and cross-referenced with World Shipping Council. Page H1 is 'List of busiest container ports' (no 'world's' prefix; the article does NOT split operational vs under-construction — all ranked entries are operational). The master article enumerates 100 ports per Lloyd's List; staged 20 are the top-20 subset by 2024 TEU.

Per-port Wikipedia articles (per-row entity-detail grounding for Country + City; TEU value is staged from master per the canonical-source rule inversion):
- source_urls[1] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Shanghai): Country = China; City = Shanghai. Per-port infobox cites TEU 43.3M (2019) which is stale by 5 years — staged value 51.5M follows master 2024 column per canonical-source rule inversion.
- source_urls[2] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Singapore): Country = Singapore (city-state, Country and City both 'Singapore'); City = Singapore. Per-port has INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY (infobox 37.2M from 2019 vs body table 41.1M from 2024); master 41.1M agrees with per-port body. Staged 41.1M.
- source_urls[3] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Ningbo-Zhoushan): Country = China; City = Ningbo (primary city of the Ningbo + Zhoushan port conglomeration; per-port article title uses hyphenated form but the dominant city per article lead is Ningbo; Zhoushan is the secondary partner city in Zhejiang province — staged 'Ningbo' as the single-cell City value, with Zhoushan acknowledged in open_questions). Per-port body TEU 16.83M from 2012 is heavily stale — staged 39.3M follows master 2024.
- source_urls[4] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Shenzhen): Country = China; City = Shenzhen. Per-port body 30.0M (2022) is slightly stale — staged 33.4M follows master 2024.
- source_urls[5] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qingdao_Port): Country = China; City = Qingdao. Note: Wikipedia article title is 'Qingdao Port' (no 'Port of' prefix — staged Wikipedia common-form name with the suffix-form preserved per article title; 'Port of Qingdao' is a redirect). Per-port article has no TEU figure in infobox or body — master 30.9M is the only sourced value.
- source_urls[6] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Guangzhou): Country = China; City = Guangzhou. Per-port body 4.774M (2006) is heavily stale — staged 26.1M follows master 2024.
- source_urls[7] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Busan): Country = South Korea; City = Busan. Per-port body 24.4M (2024) AGREES with master 24.4M (2024) — no inversion needed.
- source_urls[8] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Tianjin): Country = China; City = Tianjin. Per-port 13M (2013) is heavily stale — staged 23.3M follows master 2024.
- source_urls[9] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Jebel_Ali): Country = United Arab Emirates; City = Dubai (Jebel Ali is a deep-water port located in the Jebel Ali area of Dubai per per-port article lead). Note: master article uses 'Jebel Ali Dubai' as port name; staged form 'Port of Jebel Ali' follows Wikipedia article title. Per-port 13.7M (2021) is stale — staged 15.5M follows master 2024.
- source_urls[10] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_Klang): Country = Malaysia; City = Klang (Klang is the city in Selangor state). Note: Wikipedia article title is 'Port Klang' (no 'Port of' prefix; the toponym 'Port Klang' is the official name). Per-port article has no TEU figure — master 14.6M is the only sourced value.
- source_urls[11] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Rotterdam): Country = Netherlands; City = Rotterdam. Per-port 15.3M (2021) is stale — staged 13.8M follows master 2024 (note: this is the only port where 2024 TEU is LOWER than the per-port stale value, reflecting Rotterdam's actual decline in throughput post-2021).
- source_urls[12] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Hong_Kong): Country = China (per master-list grouping rule); City = Hong Kong. Note: Hong Kong listed separately as its own row in master article with flag PRC; staged Country = China per master-list grouping (mirrors cycle-1 bridges Stonecutters-Hong-Kong-to-China precedent). Per-port has INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY (infobox 18M from 2020 vs body 23.9M from 2007 peak); staged 13.7M follows master 2024.
- source_urls[13] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Antwerp): Country = Belgium; City = Antwerp. Note: Antwerp-Bruges merger occurred 2022; both 'Port of Antwerp' (legacy article, used by master ranking) and 'Port of Antwerp-Bruges' (post-merger authority) exist as separate Wikipedia articles. Staged form 'Port of Antwerp' matches master article naming. Per-port 13.4M (2023) is mildly stale — staged 13.5M follows master 2024.
- source_urls[14] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Tanjung_Pelepas): Country = Malaysia; City = Iskandar Puteri (located in Iskandar Puteri, Johor state). Per-port 11.2M (2021) is stale — staged 12.3M follows master 2024.
- source_urls[15] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Xiamen): Country = China; City = Xiamen (Fujian province). Per-port 8.08M (2013) is heavily stale — staged 12.3M follows master 2024.
- source_urls[16] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Los_Angeles): Country = United States; City = Los Angeles (San Pedro neighborhood per per-port infobox). Per-port infobox 10.3M (2024) AGREES with master 10.3M (2024); per-port body lags at 9.3M (2019) — staged 10.3M.
- source_urls[17] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanger_Med): Country = Morocco; City = Tangier (port is located ~45 km east-northeast of Tangier on Morocco's Mediterranean coast per per-port article; canonical association city is Tangier). Note: Wikipedia article title is 'Tanger Med' (no hyphen; 'Tanger-Med' is a redirect; master article also uses 'Tanger-Med' with hyphen — staged form follows the per-port article title without hyphen, deviating from master spelling). Per-port has no TEU throughput figure (only capacity 11M and tonnage) — master 10.2M is the only sourced TEU value.
- source_urls[18] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Long_Beach): Country = United States; City = Long Beach (California). Per-port infobox 9.7M (2024) AGREES with master 9.7M.
- source_urls[19] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Suzhou): Country = China; City = Suzhou (Jiangsu province). Note: master article uses 'Taicang/Suzhou' (Taicang is the port-district within Suzhou); per-port article uses 'Port of Suzhou' as canonical name — staged form 'Port of Suzhou' follows per-port article title. Per-port 4.45M (2014) is heavily stale — staged 9.7M follows master 2024.
- source_urls[20] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laem_Chabang): Country = Thailand; City = Laem Chabang (the locality IS the port; per-port article is the locality article with a 'Port of Laem Chabang' section). Note: Wikipedia article title is 'Laem Chabang' (no 'Port of' prefix; the locality IS the port). Per-port 7.7M (FY2017) is stale — staged 9.6M follows master 2024.

Validation note: every (Port, Country, City, TEU, Region) tuple is grounded in (a) the master 'List of busiest container ports' article confirming the port's place in the top-20 by 2024 TEU and supplying the canonical 2024 TEU value, and (b) the per-port Wikipedia article supplying Country + City via infobox/lead. Region is a curator-assigned closed-vocabulary categorical from the 9-value declared vocabulary (East Asia / Southeast Asia / South Asia / Middle East / Europe / North America / Latin America / Africa / Oceania); 6 of 9 values appear in staged data.

**Canonical-source rule (port-instance variant — explicit inversion of bridges/dams precedent for time-series metrics):** For time-series throughput metrics (TEU), master wins because Lloyd's List 2024 is fresher than per-port infoboxes which lag by 3-10 years. For non-time-series attributes (Country, City), per-port article wins (entity-detail role). For mismatch resolution: master always wins for TEU; per-port wins for Country + City when single-valued; for ambiguous City cells (Ningbo-Zhoushan conglomeration; Tanger Med located outside Tangier proper), curator-judgment picks the primary association city and documents in open_questions.

Universe-size sanity: 20 staged rows = top-20 container ports by 2024 TEU per Wikipedia master article (which enumerates 100 ports per Lloyd's List 'One Hundred Container Ports 2025'). The staged 20 cover the 9.6M-51.5M TEU range; ports below 9.6M TEU (ranks 21-100) are not staged.
decision_log:
Candidate card (Stage 1 pre-gate, then Stage 2 scored axes per instance_selection_priorities.md 4-axis rubric):
- Pre-gate verdict: PASS with four documented risks resolved at staging. R1: master vs per-port TEU value discrepancies — committed to master-wins canonical-source rule INVERSION at Stage-1 for time-series throughput metrics (the master's annual Lloyd's List update beats per-port infobox staleness). R2: Hong Kong as Country = China — committed to master-list-grouping rule at Stage-1 (mirrors cycle-1 bridges Stonecutters-Hong-Kong precedent). R3: 4 ports with non-'Port of X' Wikipedia article titles (Qingdao Port, Port Klang, Tanger Med, Laem Chabang) — committed to Wikipedia-article-title naming convention at Stage-1 (preserves diverse name forms; not all ports follow 'Port of X'). R4: 2 TEU ties (Tanjung Pelepas + Xiamen at 12.3; Long Beach + Suzhou at 9.7) — committed to TEU DESC primary + Port ASC alphabetical secondary sort at Stage-1, which inverts master-table rank for both ties. Alphabetical-secondary is the bridges/dams precedent; flagging the master-rank inversion in open_questions.
- Seed/provenance: ORIGINAL. No example_questions.txt seed addresses container ports. Closest seed-in-shape is the longest-rivers (top-K by physical dimension) seed — ports are a same-shape entity class but in an entirely different domain.
- Category: top_k (primary — single-cell-per-row attribute lookup over a fixed top-20-by-TEU entity set). Secondary: null (no clean second category; the universe is flat top-K, not partitioned).
- Source plan: 21 Wikipedia URLs (1 master + 20 per-port). Master defines universe + ranking + TEU; per-port articles supply Country + City.
- Expected shape: 20 rows × 5 cols, single PK on Port.
- Domain: Transportation/Logistics — NEW subdomain (Transportation family at 1 instance becomes 2 with Logistics NEW). Domain novelty: Good (Transportation is the most under-represented family among the 16, currently 1 instance).
- Entity-class diversity: `organizations/ports` NEW fine-class. Bucket `organizations/*` extends from 3 to 4 instances (joining universities + companies + space-agencies). Entity-class novelty: Good (NEW fine-class in mid-rep-trending-to-saturation bucket).
- 4-axis rubric scoring: Seed source Bad (Original) + Category gap Good (gap-2 chips to gap-1) + Domain novelty Good (Transportation/Logistics NEW subdomain in most under-rep family) + Entity novelty Good (NEW fine-class) = ★★★ overall.
- Risks/adaptation: per the four pre-gate risks above. Additional minor risks: (a) row count 20 is at the upper end of standard 15-25 band; (b) China dominates the top-20 ranking (9 of 20 = 45%) — same modern-engineering pattern as bridges + dams + spacecraft; (c) temporal_sensitivity = high reflects annual TEU shifts; (d) Region is curator-assigned (not directly source-grounded from per-port articles); the 9-value closed vocabulary needs explicit documentation in normalization_decisions.
- Decision: STAGE.

Further decisions:
1) Universe rule: top-20 container ports by 2024 annual TEU per Wikipedia 'List of busiest container ports' master article 2024 column (Lloyd's List sourced). All 20 are operational as of source-access date 2026-05-14. The master article enumerates 100 ports; staged 20 are the top-20 subset.
2) **Canonical-source rule INVERSION for time-series TEU metric** (Stage-1 commitment, distinct from bridges + dams which used per-entity-wins): master wins for TEU value because Lloyd's List 2024 is fresher than per-port infoboxes which lag by 3-10 years. For non-time-series attributes (Country, City), per-port article wins (entity-detail role). For Region (curator-assigned categorical), neither master nor per-port supplies the value directly — Region is a curator-mapped closed-vocab attribute documented in normalization_decisions. This inversion is justified by the time-series-vs-static distinction: TEU is an annual throughput metric the master tracks via Lloyd's List, while bridges Main Span and dams Height are structural-construction metrics that don't shift annually. The inversion is documented at Stage-1 to prevent future audit cycles from re-litigating.
3) Hong Kong handling: Port of Hong Kong staged with Country = China per master-list-grouping rule (master article lists Hong Kong separately as its own row but groups it under flag PRC). Mirrors cycle-1 bridges Stonecutters-Hong-Kong-to-China precedent. City = Hong Kong (sub-national framing preserved in City column).
4) Port name normalization: Wikipedia common-form names per article title. 16 ports follow 'Port of X' pattern; 4 exceptions follow non-'Port of' Wikipedia article titles: 'Qingdao Port' (suffix-form per article title; 'Port of Qingdao' is a redirect); 'Port Klang' (toponym is official name); 'Tanger Med' (no hyphen per Wikipedia article title; 'Tanger-Med' with hyphen is a redirect and the master article uses the hyphen — staged form follows per-port article); 'Laem Chabang' (locality article; the locality IS the port). Diacritic handling: no diacritics in staged port names (all 20 are ASCII).
5) Country values: 10 distinct countries (China 9, Malaysia 2, United States 2, plus 7 singletons for Singapore, South Korea, UAE, Netherlands, Belgium, Morocco, Thailand). All staged values are sovereign-state-level per per-port article infobox 'Country' field. UAE staged as 'United Arab Emirates' (full form per Wikipedia convention, not abbreviation 'UAE'); United States as 'United States' (not 'USA'); South Korea as 'South Korea' (not 'Republic of Korea').
6) City values: 20 distinct cities (one per port — each row has a unique City; Singapore appears as both Country and City as a city-state). Ningbo-Zhoushan conglomeration city = 'Ningbo' (primary; Zhoushan is the secondary partner — documented as open_question). Tanger Med city = 'Tangier' (canonical association city even though port is 45 km outside Tangier proper). Jebel Ali city = 'Dubai' (the emirate-city; Jebel Ali is the port-area within Dubai). Tanjung Pelepas city = 'Iskandar Puteri' (the encompassing municipality per per-port infobox).
7) TEU values: numeric metres-per-million-TEU per master article 2024 column (Lloyd's List sourced). Decimal precision: 1 (e.g., 51.5, 41.1, 13.7). All 20 staged TEU values follow master per the canonical-source rule inversion (Decision 2). Some staged values disagree with per-port infobox values which are stale by 3-10 years; documented in source_coverage_notes.
8) Region values: 9-value closed-vocab declared (East Asia / Southeast Asia / South Asia / Middle East / Europe / North America / Latin America / Africa / Oceania); 6 of 9 used in staged top-20 (South Asia, Latin America, Oceania declared for future-cycle expansion if a port from those regions enters top-20 in a future Lloyd's List update). Region is curator-assigned via a country-to-region mapping (China + Japan + South Korea + Taiwan → East Asia; Singapore + Malaysia + Indonesia + Thailand + Vietnam + Philippines → Southeast Asia; etc.). Hong Kong → East Asia per the China grouping rule.
9) Sort order: TEU (millions) DESC primary (highest-first), Port ASC alphabetical secondary tiebreaker. Two TEU ties exist: (a) at 12.3 (Tanjung Pelepas + Xiamen) where alphabetical T < X gives Tanjung Pelepas first — INVERTS master-table rank which had Xiamen at #14 and Tanjung Pelepas at #15; (b) at 9.7 (Long Beach + Suzhou) where alphabetical L < S gives Long Beach first — INVERTS master-table rank which had Suzhou at #18 and Long Beach at #19. Bridges/dams precedent uses alphabetical secondary; this is consistent across the engineered-structures and now organizations-keyed top-K instances.
10) operation_type 'filter' chosen — top-K-by-TEU is a filter operation (filter by 2024-TEU rank ≤ 20). 'aggregation' was considered (GROUP BY region) but rejected because the universe is the top-20 directly, not a per-region aggregate.
11) claim_type 'source_defined' — universe is master-article-defined top-20 by 2024 TEU. NOT `exhaustive` because the master article enumerates 100 ports (only top-20 staged). NOT `partially_supplemented` because every row + every attribute is fully grounded across master (TEU) + per-port (Country, City) + curator-assigned (Region) sources.
normalization_decisions: Port (PK) values use Wikipedia common-form names per article title. 16 of 20 ports follow 'Port of X' pattern (Port of Shanghai, Port of Singapore, Port of Ningbo-Zhoushan, Port of Shenzhen, Port of Guangzhou, Port of Busan, Port of Tianjin, Port of Jebel Ali, Port of Rotterdam, Port of Hong Kong, Port of Antwerp, Port of Tanjung Pelepas, Port of Xiamen, Port of Los Angeles, Port of Long Beach, Port of Suzhou); 4 exceptions follow non-'Port of' Wikipedia article titles: 'Qingdao Port' (suffix-form), 'Port Klang' (toponym), 'Tanger Med' (article title without hyphen, deviating from master's 'Tanger-Med'), 'Laem Chabang' (locality article). No diacritics in any staged port name (all 20 are ASCII). Country is a single categorical value per per-port article infobox 'Country' field (10 distinct values; 'United Arab Emirates' / 'United States' / 'South Korea' used in full form). City is a single categorical value per per-port article infobox 'City'/'Location' field (20 distinct values — one per port; Singapore appears as both Country and City as a city-state); conglomerate-port City staged as primary city — 'Ningbo' for Ningbo-Zhoushan, 'Iskandar Puteri' for Tanjung Pelepas, 'Tangier' for Tanger Med even though port is 45 km outside, 'Dubai' for Jebel Ali. TEU (millions) is numeric with 1 decimal precision per master article 2024 column (Lloyd's List sourced); ALL 20 staged TEU values follow master per the canonical-source rule inversion for time-series metrics (per-port infoboxes are 3-10 years stale and lose to master). Region is a curator-assigned closed-vocab categorical from a 9-value vocabulary (East Asia / Southeast Asia / South Asia / Middle East / Europe / North America / Latin America / Africa / Oceania); 6 of 9 used in staged data (South Asia, Latin America, Oceania declared for future-cycle expansion). Region assignment follows a fixed country-to-region mapping documented in decision_log Rule 8. Sort: TEU (millions) DESC primary, Port ASC alphabetical secondary.
open_questions: 1) **Canonical-source rule inversion** for time-series TEU metric: this instance inverts the bridges/dams per-entity-wins rule because TEU is annually-updated by Lloyd's List while per-port infoboxes lag by 3-10 years. The rule is justified by the time-series-vs-static distinction but an audit could challenge: should TEU also follow per-port-wins if a per-port article reports a value? Staged choice follows master because per-port infoboxes are universally stale (only 4 of 20 per-port articles have current-year TEU; the rest lag). Future audit could verify the inversion holds across all 20 rows. 2) **TEU year snapshot 2024**: master article's most-recent year is 2024 (per Lloyd's List 'One Hundred Container Ports 2025' retrieved 2025-09-18). An LLM evaluator may have parametric knowledge from earlier years (2019-2023) producing different values. temporal_sensitivity = high acknowledges this; future-cycle refresh may update to 2025 column when Lloyd's List 2026 is published. 3) **Hong Kong as Country = China**: staged per master-list-grouping rule (mirrors cycle-1 bridges Stonecutters precedent). An LLM responding 'Hong Kong' as Country is responding to the sub-national framing rather than the master-list country categorization. Both readings defensible; staged follows canonical master-list rule. 4) **Ningbo-Zhoushan City value**: staged 'Ningbo' as primary city; Zhoushan is the secondary partner city in the conglomerate port. An LLM responding 'Zhoushan' or 'Ningbo and Zhoushan' would be responding to the merged-port framing. Single-cell schema constraint forces single primary; documented exception. 5) **Tanger Med City value**: staged 'Tangier' (canonical association city) even though the port is ~45 km east-northeast of Tangier proper. An LLM responding with the precise location ('Ksar es-Seghir' or coordinates) would be more accurate geographically but less natural per the standard 'Port of [City]' framing. Staged follows the canonical-association convention. 6) **TEU ties at ranks 14-15 and 18-19**: TEU DESC + Port ASC alphabetical secondary inverts master-table rank for both ties. Staged CSV has Tanjung Pelepas before Xiamen (alphabetical T < X) but master has Xiamen first (#14, Tanjung Pelepas #15). Same for Long Beach before Suzhou (alphabetical L < S) vs master's Suzhou (#18) before Long Beach (#19). An LLM matching master rank would generate different ordering. Staged follows bridges/dams precedent of alphabetical secondary. 7) **'Port of' prefix variance**: 16 ports follow 'Port of X' pattern, 4 exceptions (Qingdao Port, Port Klang, Tanger Med, Laem Chabang) follow non-'Port of' Wikipedia article titles. An LLM responding with 'Port of Qingdao' / 'Port of Klang' / 'Port of Tanger Med' / 'Port of Laem Chabang' for the 4 exceptions would be responding to a normalized convention rather than Wikipedia article title. Staged follows Wikipedia article title per the curation convention. 8) **Tanger Med vs Tanger-Med**: master article spells with hyphen; per-port article spells without hyphen. Staged 'Tanger Med' (per per-port article title) deviates from master. An LLM responding 'Tanger-Med' would match master. Resolution: per-port-article-title wins for naming (consistent with bridges 1915 Çanakkale article-title-wins convention). 9) **Antwerp-Bruges 2022 merger**: master article uses 'Port of Antwerp' (legacy article); both 'Port of Antwerp' and 'Port of Antwerp-Bruges' Wikipedia articles still exist. Staged 'Port of Antwerp' follows master. An LLM responding 'Port of Antwerp-Bruges' would be responding to the post-merger entity. Both defensible; staged follows master-naming rule. 10) **Region as curator-assigned categorical**: Region is not directly source-grounded from per-port articles (it is a curator-applied country-to-region mapping). An LLM responding with alternative region groupings (e.g., 'Asia-Pacific' instead of 'East Asia') would be responding to alternative geographic conventions. Staged 9-value vocabulary is fixed by curator-decision documented in decision_log Rule 8.
proposed_supplements:
The 20-row staged universe is a curator-bounded subset of the world's container ports per Wikipedia master article 2024 column. Two curator-decided scope choices are documented:

(1) Top-K cutoff choice (20 vs 15 vs 30): the staged top-20 captures all ports with 9.6M+ 2024 TEU (the visible-throughput-threshold). Alternatives:
- Top-15 (15 rows): would lose Tanjung Pelepas (12.3M), Xiamen (12.3M), Los Angeles (10.3M), Tanger Med (10.2M), Long Beach (9.7M), Suzhou (9.7M), Laem Chabang (9.6M). Plausible but loses geographical balance (would over-concentrate in China + Europe + Singapore).
- Top-30 (30 rows): would add ports below 9.6M TEU. Plausible but adds row-count complexity beyond standard 15-25 band sweet spot.
- Top-20 (staged): standard sweet spot; captures meaningful geographical diversity (10 countries across 6 regions).

(2) Time-series snapshot choice (2024 vs other year): staged 2024 follows the master article's most-recent column (Lloyd's List 'One Hundred Container Ports 2025' retrieved 2025-09-18). Alternatives:
- 2023 column: would shift values modestly; preserves the same top-20 set with minor rank changes.
- Multi-year average: would smooth temporal noise but break the single-cell-per-row schema.
- Most-recent 5-year average: same as above.
2024 single-year snapshot chosen because: (a) master article foregrounds the most-recent year; (b) Lloyd's List has explicit annual reporting cadence; (c) temporal_sensitivity = high already acknowledges annual shifts.

(3) Region vocabulary choice: 9-value closed vocabulary (East Asia / Southeast Asia / South Asia / Middle East / Europe / North America / Latin America / Africa / Oceania); 6 used in staged data. Alternative regionizations:
- 'Asia-Pacific' (single value for East Asia + Southeast Asia + Oceania): would collapse 10 East Asia + 4 Southeast Asia + 0 Oceania into one bucket. Rejected as too coarse.
- UN geographic regions (more granular): would split Europe into Western/Northern/Southern/Eastern. Rejected as too granular for a top-20-row universe.
- Continental (Asia / Europe / Americas / Africa / Oceania): too coarse. Rejected.
The 9-value staged vocabulary balances granularity (distinguishes East from Southeast Asia, captures Middle East separately) with parsimony (covers all 20 staged rows with 6 values used).

This is a curator-bounded `source_defined` instance — universe is master-article-defined top-K by 2024 TEU. An audit could request expansion (top-25, top-30) or vocabulary revision based on alternative balancing.
